answer:
Pre-norm computes $x_{l+1}=x_l+F_l(N(x_l))$. The residual branch therefore retains a direct identity path through each block. Post-norm computes $x_{l+1}=N(x_l+F_l(x_l))$; even the skip path passes through a normalization Jacobian. This changes initialization-scale gradients and helps explain why some post-norm configurations need careful warmup. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.04745)

$$J_{\rm pre}=I+J_FJ_N,\qquad J_{\rm post}=J_N(I+J_F).$$

Neither formula promises perfect gradient preservation: products of many Jacobians can still amplify or shrink directions. RMSNorm versus LayerNorm is a separate choice from placement. Also, the question's model list is not uniform: Gemma 2 uses additional normalization around sublayers rather than only the simplest pre-norm layout. Check the actual architecture, depth, residual scaling, and training recipe. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07467) [4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00118)
